1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of light pulses having a first speed via an optical transmitter to a vehicle; receiving a second sequence of light pulses from the vehicle via an optical receiver; and transmitting a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the message encodes vehicle safety information including at least one of vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history, or vehicle status.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the second speed is dynamically adjusted based on proximity and motion of the vehicle.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on a loss of reception of the second sequence of light pulses and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed and is dynamically adjusted based on the third sequence of light pulses.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Original) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles.

11. (Currently Amended) An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of light pulses having a first speed via an optical transmitter to a vehicle; receive a second sequence of light pulses from the vehicle via an optical receiver; and transmit a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the message encodes vehicle safety information including at least one of vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history, or vehicle status.

13. 15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from one or more vehicles.

20.
